game.rules:
## General Game Requirements

- Any modification done to the game outside of the in-game graphics settings is NOT allowed, unless you are running categories where FPS may be changed or wish to use the *show* commands from the 2nd rule.

- Using any console commands in any build of the game is NOT allowed. The only exceptions are: *"restartlevel"*, *"show deferredlighting"*, *"show bloom"*, *"gamma [any number from 1-5]"*, *"t.maxFPS [any number from 1-60]"*, and *"slomo 1/10/100"*. [the *"slomo (10 or 100)"* command can only be used to speed up the intro cutscenes of Alpha 1 & 4 before they end, in which you use the *"slomo 1"* to revert the game speed back to normal.] You can access those commands by installing UUU [here](https://framedsc.com/GeneralGuides/universal_ue4_consoleunlocker.htm).
- Anything that is set up or performed before a run begins that ultmately benefits you during the run is NOT allowed. (This does not include changing the resolution/window size of the game, enabling the commands LISTED in the 2nd rule, or locking the frame rate as mentioned in the last rule.)
- Any macro or script activated during a completed run is NOT allowed, unless it automates a task purely for reset efficiency with no advantage or effect on the actual gameplay (i.e. having a macro that starts a New Game for you or speeds up & slows down an unskippable cutscene is allowed).
- Mapping buttons to different ones is ALLOWED as long as they only have a maximum of 1 button per input and THAT button only has 1 input. *[Reasons why you might want a key to be bound to another one is because of a broken keyboard or because you don't like the default positions of keys the game may use (WASD, E, F, etc.)].* Also, binding a button (ex: Space, F, mouse buttons, etc.) to scroll wheel is NOT allowed as the scroll wheel acts differently from every other key and cannot be "held down" or be precisely controlled, which gives the player an advantage. (Examples include using the scroll wheel to "press" Space bar at an insane rate or to "click" the mouse buttons to quickly take off nails.)
- Any strats that abuse a change in the FPS and/or lag is ALLOWED, but the frame rate that's chosen has to be put in BEFORE the run starts and CANNOT be changed mid-run [the only method that is allowed to change FPS mid-run is by freezing the game window/process]. Keep in mind that going over **75 FPS** is banned. *[Note: "Any%: No Lag Abuse" does not allow any form of FPS or lag abuse.]*

## Media Requirements

- If anything is covering any major parts of the run such as a watermark covering a big part of the screen, your run may be rejected.

- You do not need to have a timer on the screen but it is recommended.

- In-game audio is recommended for ALL runs, but if you have only microphone audio in your video, that's okay. In addition, top 3 runs may require further evidence like the raw recording file (with audio) [the only exception to the "may" portion of the sentence are world records, which require a raw file for verification]. Runs without audio at all may be rejected if deemed too suspicious.

## Timing Regarding Loads

With loads [RTA] = From start to finish without cutting out anything.

Without loads [LRT] = Not including loads.  Loads are considered to be things like the clock screen *seen in Full Game* and the screen with the "LOADING..." text *seen in Alpha 4 and the betas*.

values.rules:
- Pre-Alpha
- Any%: Beat the game. Glitches and exploits are allowed.
    - Timing starts when you open the bedroom door and ends when you OPEN the basement door, not when you unlock it. 
    - Other methods of leaving the bedroom (e.g. the floor, ceiling, etc.) are banned and your run will be rejected immediately.
        - The time the game spends on lag when getting caught will be removed from ALL runs as of 9/22/2024.
        - Console commands not listed as exceptions in the game rules are BANNED.

values.name: Any% Glitchless
values.rules:
-  Pre Alpha
    - Any% Glitchless: Beat the game without glitches.
        - Timing starts when you open the bedroom door and ends when you OPEN the basement door, not unlocking it. (Other methods of leaving the bedroom (e.g. the floor, ceiling, etc.) are banned and your run will be rejected immediately). 
        - Distracting the neighbor with an object (e.g. tv, radio or alarm clock) is not considered a glitch.
        - The time the game spends on lag when getting caught will be removed from ALL runs as of 9/22/2024.
        - Console commands not listed as exceptions in the game rules are BANNED.

- Pre-Alpha
- 100%: Beat the game by using the UV headlight to reveal the code for the keypad. Glitches are allowed.
    - Start: Depending on how you go about your run, you'll either BEGIN by sleeping repeatedly to activate the nightmare or by running towards the Neighbor's house. If you do the first option, then timing begins on any FIRST movement (WASD, mouse, or by pressing Space). If you do the second option, then timing begins when you OPEN the bedroom door to exit the house (Other methods of leaving the bedroom (e.g. the floor, ceiling, etc.) are banned and your run will be rejected immediately).
    - End: When you OPEN the door to the basement, not when you unlock it.
        - The time the game spends on lag when getting caught will be removed from ALL runs as of 9/22/2024.
        - Console commands not listed as exceptions in the game rules are BANNED.

Examples of GLITCHES: This is including but NOT limited to clipping with any objects through a wall, using an object to propel yourself into the air, or abusing the keyhole and pausing to grab objects through walls.

games.rules:
## General Game Requirements

- Any modification done to the game outside of the in-game graphics settings is NOT allowed, unless you are running categories where FPS may be changed or wish to use the *show* commands from the 2nd rule.

- Using any console commands in any build of the game is NOT allowed. The only exceptions are: *"restartlevel"*, *"show deferredlighting"*, *"show bloom"*, *"gamma [any number from 1-5]"*, *"t.maxFPS [any number from 1-60]"*, and *"slomo 1/10/100"*. [the *"slomo (10 or 100)"* command can only be used to speed up the intro cutscenes of Alpha 1 & 4 before they end, in which you use the *"slomo 1"* to revert the game speed back to normal.] You can access those commands by installing UUU [here](https://framedsc.com/GeneralGuides/universal_ue4_consoleunlocker.htm).
- Anything that is set up or performed before a run begins that ultmately benefits you during the run is NOT allowed. (This does not include changing the resolution/window size of the game, enabling the commands LISTED in the 2nd rule, or locking the frame rate as mentioned in the last rule.)
- Any macro or script activated during a completed run is NOT allowed, unless it automates a task purely for reset efficiency with no advantage or effect on the actual gameplay (i.e. having a macro that starts a New Game for you or speeds up & slows down an unskippable cutscene is allowed).
- Mapping buttons to different ones is ALLOWED as long as they only have a maximum of 1 button per input and THAT button only has 1 input. *[Reasons why you might want a key to be bound to another one is because of a broken keyboard or because you don't like the default positions of keys the game may use (WASD, E, F, etc.)].* Also, binding a button (ex: Space, F, mouse buttons, etc.) to scroll wheel is NOT allowed as the scroll wheel acts differently from every other key and cannot be "held down" or be precisely controlled, which gives the player an advantage. (Examples include using the scroll wheel to "press" Space bar at an insane rate or to "click" the mouse buttons to quickly take off nails.)
- Any strats that abuse a change in the FPS and/or lag is ALLOWED, but the frame rate that's chosen has to be put in BEFORE the run starts and CANNOT be changed mid-run [the only method that is allowed to change FPS mid-run is by freezing the game window/process]. Keep in mind that going over **75 FPS** is banned. *[Note: "Any%: No Lag Abuse" does not allow any form of FPS or lag abuse.]*

## Media Requirements

- If anything is covering any major parts of the run such as a watermark covering a big part of the screen, your run may be rejected.

- You do not need to have a timer on the screen but it is recommended.

- In-game audio is recommended for ALL runs, but if you have only microphone audio in your video, that's okay. In addition, top 3 runs may require further evidence like the raw recording file (with audio) [the only exception to the "may" portion of the sentence are world records, which require a raw file for verification]. Runs without audio at all may be rejected if deemed too suspicious.

## Timing Regarding Loads

With loads [RTA] = From start to finish without cutting out anything.

Without loads [LRT] = Not including loads.  Loads are considered to be things like the clock screen *seen in Full Game* and the screen with the "LOADING..." text *seen in Alpha 4 and the betas*.
